changes.before: To address changing operating laws and the limited ability of holding to alter departure times, this thesis proposes Bayesian Adaptive Policy Regularization (BAPR), using environment identification and operating-mode confidence adjustment, and subsequently develops Causal-Symbolic Bayesian Adaptive Policy Regularization (CS-BAPR). Across routine demand, single and repeated environmental changes, sustained high demand, and brief extreme demand, training stabilization reduces the mean headway-reward penalty relative to the preceding BAPR configuration by 58.82% to 69.79% with a single holding action. Matched comparisons with RE-SAC show tradeoffs between control reward and operational indicators, while structured policy outputs do not provide an additional benefit in every condition. With passenger-time training, generalized passenger time increases by 0.068% to 0.268% relative to the preceding BAPR configuration, so the headway gains do not extend to passenger time.
changes.after: (2) To address changes in passenger-demand and road-traffic statistics that reduce the relevance of historical experience, this thesis develops Causal-Symbolic Bayesian Adaptive Policy Regularization (CS-BAPR) based on Bayesian Adaptive Policy Regularization (BAPR). Recent rewards and disagreement among action-value estimates are used to adjust conservatism during training. Training stabilization is combined with a learnable baseline action and a neural correction, while soft symbolic constraints guide holding actions and their responses to changes in the state. Bus policies are evaluated with their trained parameters fixed. With generalized passenger time cost as the training objective, CS-BAPR reduces mean per-passenger generalized time cost by 0.083% to 0.549% relative to RE-SAC across six scenarios covering routine demand, single and repeated demand surges, sustained high demand, and brief extreme demand. Mean planned-headway deviation and forward-backward headway imbalance decrease by 7.35 to 12.09 seconds and 11.88 to 20.08 seconds, respectively. These results show average improvements over RE-SAC in passenger service and headway control under the tested demand changes.

changes.before: To reduce dependence on repeated trial-and-error data collection in the target operating environment, this thesis develops a bus-specific cross-fidelity workflow based on Hybrid Offline-and-Online Reinforcement Learning (H2O) and the Improved Framework for Hybrid Offline-and-Online Reinforcement Learning with Dynamics Gaps (H2O+). Fixed SUMO offline data and simplified-simulator interaction jointly support policy training. Simultaneous-arrival encoding, a single action that adds either no extra holding or a positive holding duration, and a completion reserve for late-operation states with low onboard loads and insufficient following service form the complete controller. In 1,350 paired evaluations covering 10 new environment blocks, three demand levels, and nine controllers, the reserve reduces within-window generalized passenger time by 92.12 seconds, or 3.71%, and increases completion by 0.466 percentage points relative to the direct parent with the same learned policy. With the same target offline data and matched actor and critic update budgets, hybrid training improves over the tested offline-only scheme.
changes.after: (3) To use existing target-environment records without relying on continued trial-and-error data collection in that environment, this thesis establishes a bus-specific cross-fidelity training procedure based on Hybrid Offline-and-Online Reinforcement Learning (H2O) and its extension, H2O+. Policies are initialized using fixed SUMO offline data and then trained further with newly collected interactions from a fast bus simulator. The bus adaptation organizes decisions for simultaneously arriving vehicles and represents both the choice of no additional holding and continuous holding durations. Across five independent training runs using the same target offline data and matched numbers of policy- and value-network updates, hybrid training reduces mean per-passenger generalized time cost by 16.66 seconds under routine demand and 19.75 seconds under 1.25-times demand relative to the tested offline-only scheme. A trip-completion safeguard is also introduced for designated operating periods when a preceding bus is present, no following bus is en route, the onboard load does not exceed 25% of capacity, and serviceable passenger demand remains. Keeping the learned policy unchanged, increasing the minimum additional holding time from 20 to 60 seconds and extending the activation period reduce mean per-passenger generalized time cost by 92.12 seconds (3.71%) and increase trip completion by 0.466 percentage points in evaluations across ten new scenario groups and demand multipliers of 0.75, 1.00, and 1.25. The two comparisons separately establish the service improvements associated with hybrid training and the execution safeguard.

The bus extension uses fixed target offline data and hybrid event models, with a normalized confidence backup limiting attenuation of model updates. With a single holding action and a passenger-time objective, generalized passenger time decreases relative to a Daganzo-style rule with the same completion reserve by 57.67, 70.67, and 76.26 seconds under calibrated, joint 50%, and joint 75% source-parameter mismatch, respectively. Joint mismatch changes road speeds, passenger OD demand, intersection delays, and required stopping-service times together. Under headway-reward training and joint 75% mismatch, MC-WM reduces generalized passenger time by 13.36 seconds relative to H2O+ with the completion reserve, but does not improve the headway reward. Benefits thus depend on both training and execution. A supplementary final-controller comparison with common source sampling and execution rules yields mean reductions of 23.02 and 40.25 seconds in generalized passenger time relative to H2O+ and source-only SAC, with completion increases of 0.1581 and 0.2626 percentage points, respectively.
changes.after: (4) To address prediction errors caused by insufficient source-simulator calibration during cross-fidelity training, this thesis proposes the Model-Corrected World Model (MC-WM). Fixed target-domain offline data are used to learn both residual corrections to source predictions and a direct target model. Prediction errors on validation data not used for model fitting determine which model generates one-step transitions for value learning. The bus model jointly predicts subsequent events, vehicle operating states, event intervals, and passenger costs. Normalized recursive confidence updates mitigate the progressive attenuation of model-sample weights. Joint source-parameter mismatches are introduced by changing road speeds, passenger OD demand, intersection delays, and required service times together. With generalized passenger time cost as the training objective, comparisons across 20 independent initializations show mean cost reductions of 51.14, 69.93, and 87.05 seconds relative to a hybrid-training baseline without a world model under calibrated, joint 50%, and joint 75% source-mismatch conditions, respectively, using the same execution rules. A separate comparison of complete controllers with matched source-interaction amounts and execution rules yields mean reductions of 23.02 seconds relative to H2O+ and 40.25 seconds relative to source-only SAC, with trip-completion increases of 0.158 and 0.263 percentage points, respectively. The results support the use of fixed target-domain offline data for model-assisted training to mitigate the effects of insufficient source calibration and improve passenger service under the tested conditions.

无折扣有限事件时域。 对第5、6章的公交任务，将运营时刻、待决策事件及终止信息纳入状态，并将终止后补齐为零奖励吸收状态。本补充允许可测状态动作空间，假定策略、奖励和转移核均可测，总变差定义为可测集合上的概率差上确界。两概率测度之差的全变差质量等于这一上确界的两倍，故式(E-15)的有界函数估计仍适用于积分形式。比较模型共用状态、动作及终止定义；在对两模型均封闭的分析范围内，另假设每条路径至多有H个决策事件，各模型每事件奖励绝对值不超过Rmax，期望即时奖励的统一误差不超过ϵr，后继事件、运行状态、事件间隔和终止信息的联合转移核总变差误差不超过ϵP。对同一固定策略，令剩余h个事件的价值误差为
eh=∥Vhπ−Vhπ∥∞,  e0=0.(E-23a)
在两个有限时域递推式之间加入并减去使用同一后继价值的中间项。即时奖励贡献至多ϵr，后继价值差贡献至多eh；剩余h个事件的价值绝对值不超过hRmax，由式(E-15)得到联合转移误差项。因此
eh+1≤ϵr+eh+2hRmaxϵP.(E-23b)
从e0=0开始对h=0,…,H−1逐项求和，使用2h=0H−1h=H(H−1)，得到
∥VHπ−VHπ∥∞≤Hϵr+H(H−1)RmaxϵP.(E-23c)
该推导不使用严格折扣，且把事件时间和结束条件包含在转移中。H是决策事件数上界，不是24,000秒运营时长；同时到站车辆的序贯选择即使不推进物理时间，也占据决策事件。现有预测均方误差不是上述联合核的总变差，已有实验也未估计统一的H、奖励界和转移误差界。因此式(E-23c)用于说明有限时域的误差传播条件，不作为已经验证的公交数值性能保证，也不将γ=1代入式(E-23)。
例如无终止、局部评分恒为0.5且γΔ=0.9时，原精确权重为0.510≈0.00098，归一化权重为0.5。该例解释的是更新强度的尺度差，固定0.5权重的对照仍须保留，不能将其改善全部归因于更准确的状态排序。

第6.4.5节的车头时距奖励补充试验采用66001、66002两个初始化，在正常标定与联合75%源偏差下新增4次MC-WM训练，并复用对应4个H2O+策略。MC-WM的模型损失系数为0.125，混合经验损失系数为0.75。各策略在两档需求、每档五个既有评价日中，分别直接执行与叠加行程完成保障，新增MC-WM评价80回合，另复用H2O+评价80回合。该组与乘客时间目标下20次独立初始化的主要比较分别统计。
